q: Vacancies in Group 'B' gazetted posts on the Railways, filled by promotion from Group 'C' staff, are ordinarily filled through the selection (seniority-cum-merit) stream to the extent of:

options.A: 30 per cent of the vacancies
options.B: 50 per cent of the vacancies
options.C: 70 per cent of the vacancies
options.D: 100 per cent of the vacancies

e: Vacancies in Group B gazetted posts filled by promotion from Group C staff are ordinarily filled 70 percent through the selection (seniority-cum-merit) stream and 30 percent through LDCE, under IREM.

q: In direct recruitment on the Railways, the relaxation admissible in the upper age limit to a candidate belonging to the category of persons with benchmark disabilities is:

options.A: 10 years
options.B: 3 years
options.C: 5 years
options.D: 15 years

e: In direct recruitment, the relaxation in upper age limit admissible to a candidate with benchmark disabilities is 10 years, as per the recruitment instructions in IREM.

q: In regard to a vacancy reserved for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in direct recruitment on the Railways, which remains unfilled for want of a suitable candidate of the reserved category, the correct position is that:

options.A: The vacancy is filled by a general category candidate by de-reserving it in the same recruitment itself
options.B: The vacancy lapses at the end of the recruitment year in all cases
options.C: The vacancy is transferred to the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination quota
options.D: De-reservation of the vacancy is not permissible in direct recruitment, and the vacancy is carried forward as a reserved vacancy in accordance with the rules

e: De-reservation of a vacancy reserved for SC or ST is not permissible in direct recruitment; an unfilled reserved vacancy is carried forward as a reserved vacancy in accordance with the rules.

q: Where the work or conduct of a railway servant on probation is not found to be satisfactory, the competent authority may:

options.A: Confirm him in the post automatically on the expiry of the original period of probation
options.B: Extend his period of probation, and thereafter discharge him from service, or revert him to his substantive post, as the case may be, if his work or conduct continues to be unsatisfactory
options.C: Impose the major penalty of dismissal on him without any order regarding his probation
options.D: Grant him a further period of probation of ten years invariably

e: Where a probationer remains unsatisfactory, the competent authority may extend his probation and thereafter discharge him from service or revert him to his substantive post, as the case may be, under IREM.

q: Staff employed in railway workshops, who are industrial employees, are granted leave with wages in accordance with:

options.A: The Leave on Average Pay rules applicable to non-industrial railway servants
options.B: The orders issued by the Railway Recruitment Board
options.C: The provisions of the Factories Act, 1948 relating to annual leave with wages
options.D: The Hours of Employment Regulations alone

e: Industrial staff in railway workshops are granted leave with wages in accordance with the annual leave with wages provisions of the Factories Act, 1948, not the LAP rules for non-industrial servants.

q: A serving railway servant who, in an emergency, undergoes medical treatment in a hospital other than a railway hospital, because no railway or Government hospital is available for the treatment required, is entitled to:

options.A: Reimbursement of the medical expenses incurred by him, subject to the prescribed conditions and ceilings
options.B: No reimbursement of any kind in any circumstances
options.C: Reimbursement only if he surrenders his medical identity card permanently
options.D: Treatment as on duty for the entire period, without any medical certificate

e: A serving railway servant who in an emergency takes treatment in a non-railway hospital because no railway or Government hospital is available is entitled to reimbursement of medical expenses, subject to prescribed conditions and ceilings, under the medical rules in IREM.

q: Where a railway servant is transferred permanently from one Railway to another Railway, the balance at his credit in the Provident Fund is:

options.A: Paid to him in cash at the time of his transfer in all cases
options.B: Forfeited to the Railway from which he is transferred
options.C: Credited to the Staff Benefit Fund of the transferring Railway
options.D: Transferred, along with his Provident Fund account, to the Accounts Office of the Railway to which he is transferred

e: On permanent transfer from one Railway to another, the Provident Fund balance is not paid out or forfeited; the PF account and balance are transferred to the Accounts Office of the Railway to which he is transferred.

q: For ensuring compliance with the instructions relating to reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in railway services, the officer appointed in a Railway administration to watch the proper implementation of the reservation orders and to maintain liaison in the matter is the:

options.A: Presenting Officer
options.B: Liaison Officer
options.C: Inquiring Authority
options.D: Public Information Officer

e: The Liaison Officer is appointed in a Railway administration to watch proper implementation of reservation orders for SC, ST and OBC and to maintain liaison in the matter, under IREM.

q: Promotion of a railway servant to a non-selection post is made on the basis of seniority-cum-suitability, in which the suitability of the railway servant is assessed:

options.A: By a competitive written examination held among all the staff in the feeder grade
options.B: By the recognised trade union of the cadre
options.C: By the Departmental Promotion Committee, on the basis of the service records of the railway servant, subject to his being found suitable for promotion
options.D: Solely on the basis of the marks obtained by him in the last departmental examination

e: Promotion to a non-selection post is by seniority-cum-suitability, the suitability being assessed by the Departmental Promotion Committee on the basis of service records, subject to the servant being found suitable, under IREM.

q: The Staff Benefit Fund on the Railways is administered:

options.A: Through Staff Benefit Fund Committees constituted at the prescribed levels of the Railway administration
options.B: Personally by the General Manager of each zonal Railway, without any committee
options.C: By the Railway Recruitment Boards of the respective zones
options.D: By the recognised trade unions of railway employees alone

e: The Staff Benefit Fund on the Railways is administered through Staff Benefit Fund Committees constituted at the prescribed levels of the Railway administration, under IREM.

q: A financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression scheme is granted to a railway servant:

options.A: Automatically by the Accounts Office, without any assessment of his performance
options.B: On the recommendation of the recognised trade union of his cadre
options.C: Only after a written examination conducted for the purpose
options.D: After screening by a Screening Committee constituted for the purpose, on the basis of the prescribed benchmark of grading in his Annual Performance Appraisal Reports

e: A financial upgradation under MACP is granted only after screening by a Screening Committee on the basis of the prescribed APAR grading benchmark; it is not automatic or examination-based.

q: A railway servant who proceeds on leave for a period of not less than thirty days may be allowed, before proceeding on the leave:

options.A: An advance equal to six months' pay in all cases
options.B: An advance of his leave salary, up to the amount of leave salary and allowances admissible to him for the first thirty days of the leave
options.C: The entire salary for the period of leave, without any adjustment thereafter
options.D: No advance of any kind, as advances against leave salary are prohibited

e: A railway servant proceeding on leave of not less than 30 days may be allowed an advance of leave salary up to the leave salary and allowances admissible for the first 30 days of the leave, under the leave rules in IREM.

q: Maternity leave admissible to a female railway servant who herself bears a child as a surrogate mother, having less than two surviving children, is:

options.A: Not admissible in any circumstances
options.B: Admissible for a maximum of 45 days only
options.C: Admissible for 180 days, as in the case of a normal delivery
options.D: Admissible only with the personal sanction of the Railway Board

e: Under the amended leave rules, maternity leave of 180 days is admissible to a female railway servant who herself bears a child as a surrogate mother, having less than two surviving children, as in a normal delivery.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 14 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 38,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:
e: Death gratuity slab for 11 to 20 years of qualifying service is 20 times emoluments: 14 years falls in this slab, so 20 x Rs 38,000 = Rs 7,60,000.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 9 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 52,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity, where pension is not admissible, is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period: 9 years = 18 periods, so 18 x Rs 26,000 = Rs 4,68,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 18 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 44,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of monthly emoluments per completed six-monthly period: 18 years = 36 periods, so 36 x (Rs 44,000 / 4) = 36 x Rs 11,000 = Rs 3,96,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 36,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: NPS employee contribution is 10 percent of basic pay plus DA: basic plus DA = Rs 36,000 + Rs 18,000 = Rs 54,000, and 10 percent of Rs 54,000 = Rs 5,400.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 52,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 15,600 per month
options.B: Rs 26,000 per month
options.C: Rs 20,800 per month
options.D: Rs 10,400 per month

e: Normal rate family pension under the RS (Pension) Rules is 30 percent of last basic pay: 30 percent of Rs 52,000 = Rs 15,600 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation under the Unified Pension Scheme after rendering 22 years of qualifying service. His last drawn basic pay is Rs 50,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The lump sum payment admissible to him, at the rate of one-tenth of his last drawn basic pay plus dearness allowance for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: UPS lump sum is one-tenth of last basic pay plus DA per completed six-monthly period: one-tenth of Rs 75,000 = Rs 7,500, and 22 years = 44 periods, so 44 x Rs 7,500 = Rs 3,30,000.

q: House Building Advance admissible to a railway servant can also be utilised by him for:

options.A: Meeting the expenditure on the marriage of his children
options.B: The purchase of a plot of land for the construction of a house by him, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.C: The purchase of a motor car for his personal use
options.D: Investment in shares and securities

e: House Building Advance may also be utilised, subject to prescribed conditions, for purchase of a plot of land for construction of a house by the railway servant, under the HBA rules in IREM.

q: A railway pensioner dies within five years of his retirement. The total amount of pension and retirement gratuity actually drawn by him is less than twelve times his emoluments. In such a case, his nominee or family becomes entitled to:

options.A: A second full retirement gratuity
options.B: Residuary gratuity equal to the difference between twelve times the emoluments and the pension and gratuity already drawn
options.C: Only the balance at his credit in the Provident Fund
options.D: No further amount, as gratuity is payable only once

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, residuary gratuity is payable to the nominee or family where the pensioner dies within five years of retirement and the pension and retirement gratuity drawn total less than 12 times his emoluments, equal to that difference.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 16 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 58,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: Death gratuity slab for 11 to 20 years of qualifying service is 20 times emoluments: 16 years falls in this slab, so 20 x Rs 58,000 = Rs 11,60,000.

q: The 'right to information' under the Right to Information Act, 2005 includes the right to:

options.A: Obtain certified samples of material held by the public authority
options.B: Direct the public authority to create new records for the applicant
options.C: Inspect the private residence of a public servant
options.D: Demand information on any matter pending before a court, in all cases

e: Under Section 2(j) of the RTI Act, the right to information includes the right to obtain certified samples of material held by the public authority; it does not extend to directing creation of new records.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than the following period without an interval for rest of at least half an hour:

options.A: Three hours
options.B: Four hours
options.C: Five hours
options.D: Six hours

e: Under Section 54 of the Factories Act read with the rest-interval provision, no adult worker shall work for more than five hours in a factory without an interval for rest of at least half an hour.

q: In regard to paternity leave admissible to a male railway servant, the correct position is that the leave:

options.A: Is debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Cannot be combined with any other kind of leave
options.C: Is not debited to his leave account and may be combined with any other kind of leave due and admissible to him
options.D: Can be availed of only after the child attains the age of one year

e: Paternity leave is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay account of a male railway servant and may be combined with any other kind of leave due and admissible, under the leave rules in IREM.

q: Under Rule 4 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Permit his son or daughter to accept any employment whatsoever
options.B: Use his position or influence, directly or indirectly, to secure employment for any member of his family in any private undertaking
options.C: Allow any member of his family to reside with him
options.D: Send his children to a private school

e: Under Rule 4 of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not use his position or influence, directly or indirectly, to secure employment for any family member in any private undertaking.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 21 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 66,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him is:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of monthly emoluments per completed six-monthly period: 21 years = 42 periods, so 42 x (Rs 66,000 / 4) = 42 x Rs 16,500 = Rs 6,93,000, which is within the 16.5 times emoluments ceiling.

q: Information, the disclosure of which would cause a breach of privilege of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State, is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(a)
options.B: Section 8(1)(c)
options.C: Section 8(1)(e)
options.D: Section 8(1)(j)

e: Information whose disclosure would cause a breach of privilege of Parliament or of a State Legislature is exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, every dangerous part of any machinery in a factory is required to be:

options.A: Securely fenced by safeguards of substantial construction, which shall be maintained and kept in position while the parts of the machinery are in motion or in use
options.B: Painted red and marked with a warning board only
options.C: Operated only by the foreman of the shop
options.D: Covered with a cloth screen during working hours

e: Under Section 21 of the Factories Act, every dangerous part of machinery must be securely fenced by safeguards of substantial construction, maintained and kept in position while the parts are in motion or in use.

q: An application by an employed person to the Authority appointed under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, for a direction to the employer to refund an unauthorised deduction from his wages, or to pay the wages delayed, must ordinarily be made within:

options.A: Three months from the date of the deduction or delay
options.B: Six months from the date of the deduction or delay
options.C: Twelve months from the date of the deduction or delay
options.D: Three years from the date of the deduction or delay

e: Under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, an application for refund of an unauthorised deduction or payment of delayed wages must ordinarily be made within 12 months from the date of the deduction or delay.

q: Leave Not Due is admissible only to the following class of railway servants:

options.A: Temporary railway servants
options.B: Permanent railway servants
options.C: Casual labour who have been granted temporary status
options.D: Substitutes engaged on the Railways

e: Leave Not Due under the leave rules in IREM is admissible only to permanent railway servants, not to temporary servants, casual labour with temporary status or substitutes.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 52,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution of the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance, is:
e: NPS Government contribution is 14 percent of basic pay plus DA: basic plus DA = Rs 52,000 + Rs 26,000 = Rs 78,000, and 14 percent of Rs 78,000 = Rs 10,920.

q: Under Section 8(2) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, a public authority may allow access to information, notwithstanding the exemptions contained in Section 8(1), where:

options.A: The applicant agrees to pay double the prescribed fee
options.B: The applicant is a Member of Parliament
options.C: The information sought is more than ten years old
options.D: The public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests

e: Under Section 8(2) of the RTI Act, a public authority may allow access to information despite the Section 8(1) exemptions where the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests.

q: A period of absence of a railway servant is treated as 'dies non'. The effect of such treatment is that:

options.A: His past service rendered before the period is forfeited for pension
options.B: The period constitutes a break in his service for all purposes
options.C: The period itself counts neither for increment nor for pension, but it does not entail forfeiture of his past service
options.D: He is entitled to half leave salary for the period

e: A period treated as dies non counts neither for increment nor for pension, but it does not entail forfeiture of past service or constitute a break in service, under IREM.

q: A railway servant who is promoted to a higher group during the course of a year becomes liable to pay the subscription of the higher group under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme:

options.A: From the month following his promotion
options.B: From the 1st January of the year following the year of his promotion
options.C: From the date of his next annual increment
options.D: Only from the 1st April of the next financial year

e: Under the CGEGIS rules, a railway servant promoted to a higher group becomes liable to pay the higher group subscription from the 1st January of the year following the year of his promotion.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the periods of work for adult workers in a factory are required to be:

options.A: Communicated orally to each worker by the foreman
options.B: Decided afresh every day by the manager of the factory
options.C: Recorded only in the muster roll of the workshop
options.D: Fixed beforehand and exhibited in the factory by means of a notice of periods of work, displayed in the prescribed form

e: Under the Factories Act, periods of work for adult workers must be fixed beforehand and exhibited in the factory by a notice of periods of work displayed in the prescribed form.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 5 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 42,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, is:
e: Service gratuity, where pension is not admissible, is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period: 5 years = 10 periods, so 10 x Rs 21,000 = Rs 2,10,000.

q: A request for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 may be rejected by the Central Public Information Officer where the disclosure of the information would involve:

options.A: Embarrassment to the public authority
options.B: Criticism of a decision taken by the public authority
options.C: An infringement of copyright subsisting in a person other than the State
options.D: Disclosure of the file notings made on the file

e: Under Section 9 of the RTI Act, a CPIO may reject a request where disclosure of the information would involve an infringement of copyright subsisting in a person other than the State.

q: Under the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, unless it is otherwise expressly provided:

options.A: The whole time of a railway servant is at the disposal of the Government (Railway Administration) which employs him
options.B: A railway servant may take up private work in his spare time without any sanction
options.C: A railway servant is required to work only during the prescribed office hours
options.D: A railway servant may hold a second employment during his leave without any sanction

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, unless otherwise expressly provided, the whole time of a railway servant is at the disposal of the Government or Railway Administration which employs him.

q: A retired railway servant engaged as a defence assistant by a charged railway servant in departmental inquiries shall not act as a defence assistant in more than the following number of cases at a time:

options.A: Three cases
options.B: Five cases
options.C: Seven cases
options.D: Ten cases

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, a retired railway servant acting as defence assistant shall not act as defence assistant in more than seven cases at a time.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 280 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 54,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Cash equivalent of leave salary = (basic pay + DA) / 30 x LAP days = (Rs 54,000 + Rs 27,000) / 30 x 280 = Rs 2,700 x 280 = Rs 7,56,000.

q: The general penalty for a contravention of the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948, for which no penalty is separately provided in the Act, is:

options.A: Fine up to Rs 10,000 only
options.B: Imprisonment for a term up to three months only
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or both
options.D: Imprisonment for a term up to five years and fine up to five lakh rupees

e: Under Section 92 of the Factories Act, the general penalty for a contravention with no separately provided penalty is imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.

q: The additional quantum of pension admissible on attaining the age of 80 years and above is payable:

options.A: Only on the pension of the railway pensioner, and not on family pension
options.B: Only where the family pension is drawn at the enhanced rate
options.C: Only to a widow family pensioner, and to no other family pensioner
options.D: On family pension also, to a family pensioner who has attained the prescribed age

e: The additional quantum of pension on attaining 80 years and above is payable on family pension also, to a family pensioner who has attained the prescribed age, under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a contract or agreement by which an employed person relinquishes, or reduces, any right conferred on him by the Act is:

options.A: Null and void in so far as it purports to remove or reduce the liability of any person to pay wages in accordance with the Act
options.B: Valid if it is registered with the registering authority
options.C: Valid if the employed person has agreed to it in writing
options.D: Valid in the case of employees drawing higher wages

e: Under Section 23 of the Payment of Wages Act, a contract or agreement by which an employed person relinquishes or reduces any right under the Act is null and void to that extent.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 72,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last pay drawn, is:

options.A: Rs 18,000 per month
options.B: Rs 21,600 per month
options.C: Rs 24,000 per month
options.D: Rs 36,000 per month

e: Normal rate family pension under the RS (Pension) Rules is 30 percent of last pay drawn: 30 percent of Rs 72,000 = Rs 21,600 per month.

q: The Central Information Commission under the Right to Information Act, 2005 consists of:

options.A: The Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners
options.B: The Chief Information Commissioner and not more than five Information Commissioners
options.C: The Chief Information Commissioner and exactly ten Information Commissioners
options.D: The Chief Information Commissioner alone

e: Under Section 12 of the RTI Act, the Central Information Commission consists of the Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners.

q: A railway servant who is declared surplus in his cadre and is absorbed in an alternative post in a different seniority unit is assigned seniority in the new unit:

options.A: With reference to his original date of appointment in the parent cadre, in all cases
options.B: Below all the direct recruits of the preceding five years in the new unit
options.C: Only after he completes five years of service in the new unit
options.D: From the date of his absorption in the new unit, his past service in the parent cadre not counting for seniority in the new unit

e: A surplus railway servant absorbed in an alternative post in a different seniority unit gets seniority in the new unit from the date of his absorption, his past service in the parent cadre not counting for seniority there, under IREM.

q: Commuted leave without a medical certificate may be granted to a railway servant, against the Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit, where the leave is required for an approved course of study, up to a maximum of:

options.A: 60 days during his entire service
options.B: 90 days during his entire service
options.C: 120 days during his entire service
options.D: 180 days during his entire service

e: Commuted leave without a medical certificate may be granted against LHAP at credit for an approved course of study up to a maximum of 180 days during the entire service, under the leave rules in IREM.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an employer is liable to pay compensation to an employee where:

options.A: The employee suffers any illness, whether or not it is connected with his employment
options.B: Personal injury is caused to the employee by an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment
options.C: The employee is transferred to a distant station against his wishes
options.D: The employee retires from service on attaining the age of superannuation

e: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the employer is liable to pay compensation where personal injury is caused to an employee by an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment.

q: The commuted portion of the pension of a railway pensioner has been restored to him after the expiry of fifteen years. He now applies for commutation of a further portion of his pension. The correct position is that:

options.A: He may commute up to 40 per cent of his pension afresh
options.B: He may commute up to 20 per cent of his pension afresh
options.C: No further commutation of pension is permissible to him
options.D: Fresh commutation is permissible only after he undergoes a medical examination

e: Under the Commutation Rules, once the commuted portion of pension has been restored after 15 years, no further commutation of pension is permissible to the pensioner.

q: 'Worker', as defined in the Factories Act, 1948, means a person employed in a manufacturing process or in work incidental to it, and includes a person employed:

options.A: Only directly by the occupier of the factory
options.B: Directly or by or through any agency, including a contractor, with or without the knowledge of the principal employer
options.C: Only against a permanent post in the factory
options.D: Only if he is a member of a recognised trade union

e: Section 2(l) of the Factories Act, 1948 defines a worker as a person employed in a manufacturing process or work incidental to it, directly or by or through any agency, including a contractor, with or without the knowledge of the principal employer.

q: A railway pensioner who has opted for Fixed Medical Allowance in lieu of the outpatient treatment facility under the health scheme remains entitled to:

options.A: Indoor (in-patient) treatment in a railway hospital, the allowance being in lieu of outpatient treatment only
options.B: No medical treatment of any kind in a railway hospital
options.C: Treatment only in a private hospital, entirely at his own cost
options.D: Outpatient treatment in a railway hospital in addition to the allowance

e: Fixed Medical Allowance is paid in lieu of outpatient (OPD) treatment only under the railway health scheme. In-patient or indoor treatment in a railway hospital is not surrendered by opting for the allowance, so that facility remains available to the pensioner.

q: 'PREM', a forum functioning on the Railways for consultation with railway employees, stands for:

options.A: Permanent Railway Employees Machinery
options.B: Programme for Railway Employees' Motivation
options.C: Panel of Railway Experts and Managers
options.D: Participation of Railway Employees in Management

e: PREM stands for Participation of Railway Employees in Management. It is the consultative forum on the Railways through which representatives of railway employees participate in discussions with management on matters of mutual interest.

q: Where the competent authority decides to extend the period of probation of a railway servant on account of his unsatisfactory work or conduct, the extension so granted at a time should ordinarily not exceed:

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: One year
options.D: Two years

e: Under the Railway Services rules on probation, where probation is extended for unsatisfactory work or conduct, the extension granted at a time should ordinarily not exceed one year, and the probationer must be informed of the period and the conditions.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, railway staff may be temporarily exempted from the provisions relating to hours of work and periods of rest where:

options.A: The staff themselves volunteer in writing to work longer hours
options.B: The Railway is short of staff for administrative reasons
options.C: Overtime allowance is paid to the staff for the extra hours worked
options.D: An accident or emergency, or work of an urgent nature, so requires

e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, temporary exemption from the provisions on hours of work and rest is permitted only in cases of accident or emergency, or where work of an urgent nature so requires, not merely for staff shortage or on payment of overtime.

q: Reservation for Other Backward Classes in direct recruitment on the Railways is admissible to a candidate only where:

options.A: His caste is notified in the Central List of Other Backward Classes in respect of the State to which he belongs
options.B: His caste is included in the State list of backward classes maintained for State Government services
options.C: His family income is below the creamy layer limit, irrespective of the list in which his caste appears
options.D: He obtains a certificate from the Gram Panchayat of his village

e: Reservation for OBCs in direct recruitment is governed by the Central List of OBCs. The candidate's caste must be notified in the Central List in respect of the State to which he belongs; inclusion only in a State list for State services does not qualify him.

q: In regard to the grant of leave to a railway servant who is under suspension, the correct position is that:

options.A: He may be granted Leave on Average Pay at the discretion of the leave sanctioning authority
options.B: He may be granted only casual leave during the period of suspension
options.C: Leave cannot be granted to a railway servant under suspension
options.D: He may be granted leave without pay as a matter of course

e: Under the Railway Services (Pension) and Leave rules, leave cannot be granted to a railway servant who is under suspension. The period of suspension is dealt with separately on conclusion of the proceedings and is not converted into leave on request during suspension.

q: Family pension at the enhanced rate, of 50 per cent of the last pay drawn, is admissible on the death of a railway servant in service only where he had rendered, before his death, a minimum continuous service of:

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 5 years
options.C: No minimum period of service is required
options.D: 10 years

e: The seven-year condition stands removed: family pension at the enhanced rate of 50 per cent of last pay is admissible on death in service even if the railway servant died within seven years of joining, so no minimum continuous service is required. (Source: Rule 54, CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 amended by notification dated 19.09.2019, and Rule 75(4A) of the RS (Pension) Rules inserted by the Second Amendment Rules, 2024 (RBE No. 77/2024); effective 01.10.2019).

q: A railway servant is retired from service on invalid pension, on being declared by the competent medical authority to be permanently incapacitated for further service, after rendering only six years of qualifying service. In regard to his pensionary benefit, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is entitled only to service gratuity, pension being inadmissible with less than ten years of qualifying service
options.B: He is entitled to invalid pension at 50 per cent of his emoluments or average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial (minimum Rs 9,000 per month), even though his qualifying service is less than ten years
options.C: He is entitled to full pension as admissible on superannuation
options.D: He is entitled to no retirement benefit of any kind

e: Invalid pension is admissible even with less than ten years of qualifying service where the servant is permanently incapacitated, and it is calculated at 50 per cent of emoluments or average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial, subject to the minimum pension of Rs 9,000 per month.

q: The Chief Information Commissioner under the Right to Information Act, 2005 may be removed from his office by the President:

options.A: At any time, without assigning any reason
options.B: On the recommendation of the Central Vigilance Commission alone
options.C: Only after he attains the age of 65 years
options.D: Only on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, after the Supreme Court has, on a reference made to it by the President, held an inquiry and reported that he ought to be removed

e: Section 14 of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that the Chief Information Commissioner can be removed by the President only on proved misbehaviour or incapacity, after the Supreme Court, on a reference from the President, has inquired and reported that he ought to be removed.

q: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 does not apply to a railway servant because:

options.A: Railways are not an establishment for any purpose under the Act
options.B: Gratuity is not payable to railway servants at all
options.C: A railway servant holds a post under the Central Government and his gratuity is governed by the pension rules applicable to him
options.D: The Act applies only to employees of State Governments

e: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 does not apply to railway servants because they hold posts under the Central Government and their gratuity is governed by the RS (Pension) Rules applicable to them, which is the ground of exclusion in Section 2(e) read with the Act.

q: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity received by a railway servant, a Government employee, is, under the Income-tax Act:

options.A: Fully taxable as income from salaries
options.B: Fully exempt from income tax
options.C: Exempt only to the extent of Rs 10 lakh
options.D: Exempt only to the extent of Rs 20 lakh

e: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity received by a Government employee is fully exempt from income tax under Section 10(10)(i) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. The monetary ceilings in the Act apply to non-Government employees, not to Government servants.

q: Pre-promotion training on the Railways is imparted to:

options.A: Employees belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in the zone of consideration for selection posts, so as to improve their performance in the selection
options.B: All railway servants in the zone of consideration for every selection
options.C: Only gazetted officers posted in training institutes
options.D: Only direct recruits during their period of probation

e: Pre-promotion training is a special measure under the reservation instructions: it is imparted to SC and ST employees in the zone of consideration for selection posts so as to improve their performance in the selection, and is not a general training for all candidates.

q: In regard to family pension admissible to a spouse who married the railway servant after his retirement, that is, a post-retiral marriage, the correct position is that:

options.A: Family pension is admissible to such a spouse on the death of the pensioner
options.B: Family pension is not admissible to such a spouse in any circumstances
options.C: Family pension is admissible only if the marriage took place within one year of the retirement
options.D: Family pension is admissible only with the previous sanction of the Railway Board

e: Family pension is admissible to a spouse married to the railway servant after his retirement. Post-retiral spouses were brought within the definition of family for family pension, so on the pensioner's death such a spouse is eligible, subject to the usual conditions.

q: In regard to a temporary (refundable) advance drawn by a railway servant from the amount at his credit in the Provident Fund, the correct position is that:

options.A: Interest is charged on the advance at the rate applicable to House Building Advance
options.B: Interest is charged on the advance at the rate of interest allowed on Provident Fund accumulations
options.C: Interest is charged on the advance at a flat rate of six per cent per annum
options.D: No interest is charged on the advance

e: A temporary advance from the Provident Fund is refundable by recovery in instalments, but no interest is charged on it. Interest is earned on the balance in the fund; the advance itself carries no interest liability for the subscriber.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 8 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 46,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments, will be:
e: Death after 8 years falls in the 5-11 years slab, so death gratuity is 12 x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules. Computation: 12 x Rs 46,000 = Rs 5,52,000.

q: Under Section 10 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where a request for information is rejected in part on the ground that a portion of the record is exempt from disclosure, access may be provided to the applicant to:

options.A: That part of the record which does not contain any information exempt from disclosure and which can reasonably be severed from any part that contains exempt information
options.B: The whole record, as severance of a record is not permissible under the Act
options.C: No part of the record, as partial disclosure is prohibited
options.D: The exempt part of the record only, after deleting the non-exempt part

e: Section 10 of the RTI Act, 2005 expressly permits severability: access may be given to that part of the record which does not contain exempt information and which can reasonably be severed from the part containing exempt information.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the occupier of a factory shall send a written notice to the Chief Inspector of Factories, containing the prescribed particulars of the factory, at least the following period before he begins to occupy or use any premises as a factory:

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 45 days

e: Section 7 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the occupier to send written notice of the prescribed particulars to the Chief Inspector at least 15 days before he begins to occupy or use any premises as a factory.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 30 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 57,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: 30 years give 60 six-monthly periods; retirement gratuity is 1/4 x emoluments per period, that is 60 x 1/4 = 15 months of emoluments, within the 16.5 x maximum. Computation: 15 x Rs 57,000 = Rs 8,55,000.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the wage period fixed by every person responsible for the payment of wages to employed persons shall not exceed:

options.A: One week
options.B: One fortnight
options.C: One month
options.D: Two months

e: Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 requires wages to be paid before the prescribed day following the wage period, and the wage period fixed by the person responsible for payment shall not exceed one month.

q: For the purpose of computing retirement gratuity and death gratuity under the pension rules applicable to railway servants, the emoluments reckoned are:

options.A: The pay drawn by the railway servant, together with the dearness allowance admissible thereon
options.B: The pay drawn by the railway servant alone, dearness allowance being never reckoned for any pensionary benefit
options.C: The average monthly pay earned by the railway servant during the last three years of his service
options.D: The pay drawn by the railway servant, together with all allowances including house rent allowance

e: For retirement and death gratuity under the RS (Pension) Rules, emoluments mean the pay drawn together with the dearness allowance admissible on it at the relevant date. House rent and other allowances are not reckoned.

q: Under Section 16 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in a factory built after the commencement of the Act, every workroom shall be of sufficient capacity so as to allow for every worker employed in it a space of at least:

options.A: 4.2 cubic metres
options.B: 9.9 cubic metres
options.C: 20 cubic metres
options.D: 14.2 cubic metres

e: Section 16 of the Factories Act, 1948 fixes overcrowding limits: in a factory built after commencement of the Act, every workroom must allow at least 14.2 cubic metres of space for every worker employed in it (9.9 cubic metres applies to older factories).

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 44,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at the rate of 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus dearness allowance, will be:
e: NPS Tier-I contribution of the employee is 10 per cent of basic pay plus DA. Pay plus DA = Rs 44,000 + 50 per cent of Rs 44,000 = Rs 66,000. Computation: 10 per cent of Rs 66,000 = Rs 6,600 per month.

q: Where the Central Public Information Officer fails to give a decision on a request for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 within the period specified for the purpose, the position under Section 7(2) of the Act is that the Central Public Information Officer shall be:

options.A: Deemed to have granted the request for information
options.B: Transferred from the post of Central Public Information Officer
options.C: Deemed to have refused the request for information
options.D: Required to obtain the orders of the Central Information Commission before deciding the request

e: Section 7(2) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that if the CPIO fails to give a decision within the specified period, he shall be deemed to have refused the request, and the applicant may then proceed in appeal.

q: Under Section 18 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, effective arrangements are required to be made in every factory to provide and maintain, at suitable points conveniently situated for all workers employed therein, a sufficient supply of:

options.A: Wholesome drinking water
options.B: Tea and coffee during the intervals of rest
options.C: Water for bathing purposes only
options.D: Hot water during the winter season

e: Section 18 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires effective arrangements in every factory to provide and maintain, at suitable and convenient points, a sufficient supply of wholesome drinking water for all workers employed therein.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 7 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 48,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: With 7 years and no pension entitlement, service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. 7 years give 14 periods, that is 14 x 1/2 = 7 months. Computation: 7 x Rs 48,000 = Rs 3,36,000.

q: Dearness Relief admissible to a railway pensioner who has commuted a portion of his pension for a lump sum payment is calculated on:

options.A: The reduced pension actually drawn by him after commutation
options.B: The original basic pension, before commutation of any portion of it
options.C: The lump sum commuted value received by him
options.D: The family pension admissible to his family

e: Dearness Relief is calculated on the original basic pension before commutation, not on the reduced pension actually drawn after commutation. Commutation therefore does not reduce the pensioner's Dearness Relief.

q: The fee prescribed under the Right to Information (Fee and Cost) Rules for making an application for obtaining information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is:

options.A: Rs 2
options.B: Rs 50
options.C: Rs 10
options.D: Rs 100

e: The application fee prescribed under the RTI (Fee and Cost) Rules, 2005 for seeking information from a Central public authority is Rs 10, payable by cash, demand draft, banker's cheque or Indian Postal Order.

q: Under Section 19 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory there shall be provided a sufficient number of latrines and urinals of the prescribed types, so situated as to be convenient to the workers, and the accommodation so provided shall be:

options.A: Common to all workers, without any distinction
options.B: Provided only for the use of women workers
options.C: Located only outside the premises of the factory
options.D: Provided separately for male and female workers

e: Section 19 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires a sufficient number of latrines and urinals of the prescribed types, conveniently situated, and the accommodation must be provided separately for male and female workers.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 68,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 34,000 per month
options.B: Rs 20,400 per month
options.C: Rs 27,200 per month
options.D: Rs 40,800 per month

e: Enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn. Computation: 50 per cent of Rs 68,000 = Rs 34,000 per month.

q: A railway servant disappears, leaving his family behind, and remains untraced, a report having been lodged with the police in this regard. Subject to the prescribed conditions, family pension becomes admissible to the eligible member of his family after the expiry of the following period from the date of his disappearance:

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: Seven years

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules for a missing railway servant, family pension becomes admissible to the eligible family member after the expiry of one year from the date of disappearance, subject to a police report and the prescribed indemnity and other conditions.

q: Under Section 20 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory there shall be provided a sufficient number of spittoons at convenient places, which shall be maintained in a clean and hygienic condition, and:

options.A: Workers may spit anywhere within the premises of the factory
options.B: Spittoons are required to be provided only in the office rooms of the factory
options.C: No person shall spit within the premises of the factory except in the spittoons so provided
options.D: The spittoons are required to be cleaned only once in a year

e: Section 20 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires a sufficient number of spittoons at convenient places, maintained clean and hygienic, and provides that no person shall spit within the factory premises except in the spittoons so provided.

q: An appeal against a direction of the Authority appointed under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 lies to the District Court and is required to be preferred within a period of:

options.A: 30 days from the date of the direction
options.B: 15 days from the date of the direction
options.C: 60 days from the date of the direction
options.D: 90 days from the date of the direction

e: Section 17 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 provides an appeal to the District Court against a direction of the Authority, and the appeal must be preferred within 30 days from the date of the direction.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 240 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 45,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, worked out at the rate of pay plus dearness allowance for each day of leave divided by 30, will be:
e: Leave salary per day is (pay plus DA) divided by 30: (Rs 45,000 + Rs 22,500) / 30 = Rs 2,250 per day. Computation: Rs 2,250 x 240 days = Rs 5,40,000 as cash equivalent of leave salary.

q: A railway servant who has given notice of voluntary retirement from service may withdraw the notice, so as to continue in service:

options.A: In no case, as a notice of voluntary retirement once given can never be withdrawn
options.B: Before the date of retirement specified in the notice, with the approval of the appointing authority
options.C: At any time, even after the date of retirement specified in the notice has passed
options.D: Only with the prior approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: A notice of voluntary retirement may be withdrawn before the date of retirement specified in the notice, but only with the approval of the appointing authority. It cannot be withdrawn after that date or unilaterally as of right.

q: Under Section 28 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, every hoist and lift in a factory shall be of good mechanical construction and sound material, and shall be thoroughly examined by a competent person at least:

options.A: Once in every month
options.B: Once in every year
options.C: Once in every six months
options.D: Once in every two years

e: Section 28 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every hoist and lift to be of good construction and sound material and to be thoroughly examined by a competent person at least once in every six months.

q: Under Section 21 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is:

options.A: Done by an applicant in support of his request for information
options.B: Done by the Central Information Commission in an appeal decided by it
options.C: Done by a third party in respect of the information supplied by him
options.D: In good faith done or intended to be done under the Act or any rule made thereunder

e: Section 21 of the RTI Act, 2005 protects action taken in good faith: no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding lies against any person for anything in good faith done or intended to be done under the Act or rules made under it.

q: Which of the following is a permissible purpose for the grant of a temporary (refundable) advance to a railway servant from the amount at his credit in the General Provident Fund?

options.A: Meeting obligatory expenses in connection with betrothal, marriage, funerals or other ceremonies
options.B: Meeting the expenditure on a pleasure trip undertaken by the railway servant
options.C: Purchasing shares and securities for investment purposes
options.D: Repaying a loan taken by the railway servant from a private moneylender

e: A temporary advance from the General Provident Fund is admissible for obligatory expenses on betrothal, marriage, funerals or other ceremonies, and similar prescribed purposes. Pleasure trips, investments and repaying private loans are not permissible purposes.

q: Under Section 35 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the State Government may make rules requiring that, in respect of any manufacturing process specified in the rules, effective screens or suitable goggles shall be provided for the protection of the eyes of persons employed in the process, where the process involves:

options.A: Working in a noisy environment within the factory
options.B: Risk of injury to the eyes from particles or fragments thrown off in the course of the process, or from exposure to excessive light or heat
options.C: Working at a height above the ground level
options.D: Handling of cash and valuables in the factory office

e: Section 35 of the Factories Act, 1948 empowers rules requiring screens or suitable goggles where a process involves risk of injury to the eyes from particles or fragments thrown off, or from exposure to excessive light or heat.

q: Where a railway servant dies while in service, the members of his family who travel from the place of his death or his last headquarters to his home town or other selected place of settlement are entitled, subject to the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: No travelling concession of any kind for the journey
options.B: Only a free railway pass for the journey, without any allowance
options.C: Travelling Allowance for the journey, as admissible on transfer
options.D: Reimbursement of only one-half of the fare for the journey

e: On the death of a railway servant in service, family members travelling from the place of death or last headquarters to the home town or selected place of settlement are entitled to Travelling Allowance as admissible on transfer, subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: Under Section 23 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, no court shall entertain any suit, application or other proceeding in respect of any order made under the Act, and no such order shall be called in question otherwise than:

options.A: By a suit filed in the District Court
options.B: By a representation made to the Central Public Information Officer
options.C: By a revision petition filed before the appropriate Government
options.D: By way of an appeal under the Act

e: Section 23 of the RTI Act, 2005 bars the jurisdiction of courts: no court shall entertain any proceeding in respect of an order under the Act, and such an order can be called in question only by way of an appeal under the Act.

q: Under Section 45 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an ambulance room, of the prescribed size, containing the prescribed equipment and in the charge of such medical and nursing staff as may be prescribed, is required to be provided and maintained in every factory wherein the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than:
e: Section 45 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires an ambulance room of prescribed size, with prescribed equipment and medical and nursing staff, in every factory wherein more than 500 workers are ordinarily employed.

q: A railway servant on tour remains continuously absent from his headquarters at the same place for a period exceeding 180 days. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for the period of his absence beyond 180 days at that place is:

options.A: The full Daily Allowance
options.B: 75 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.C: 50 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.D: Nil, no Daily Allowance being admissible beyond 180 days at the same place

e: Under the Travelling Allowance rules, no Daily Allowance is admissible for the period of continuous absence from headquarters at the same place beyond 180 days. The halt beyond that limit earns no DA at full or reduced rate.

q: Under Section 62 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the manager of every factory is required to maintain a register of adult workers, showing the prescribed particulars of the workers employed in the factory, and the register shall be:

options.A: Kept in the personal custody of the occupier at his residence
options.B: Sent to the Accounts Office of the Railway for safe custody
options.C: Available to an Inspector of Factories at all times during working hours
options.D: Produced only at the time of the annual inspection of the factory

e: Section 62 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the manager to maintain a register of adult workers with the prescribed particulars, and the register must be available to the Inspector of Factories at all times during working hours.

q: Under Section 47 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, suitable shelters or rest rooms, and a suitable lunch room with provision for drinking water, where workers can eat meals brought by them, are required to be provided in every factory wherein the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than:
e: Section 47 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires suitable shelters or rest rooms and a lunch room with drinking water in every factory wherein more than 150 workers are ordinarily employed.

q: The annual report on the implementation of the provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005, which is caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, is prepared by:

options.A: The Central Information Commission and forwarded by it to the Central Government
options.B: Every public authority in respect of its own working
options.C: The Central Public Information Officer of each Ministry
options.D: The Department of Personnel and Training on its own

e: Section 25 of the RTI Act, 2005 requires the Central Information Commission to prepare an annual report on implementation of the Act and forward it to the Central Government, which causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament.

q: Under Section 18 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, every apprentice undergoing apprenticeship training in a designated trade in an establishment, such as an Act Apprentice engaged in a railway workshop, shall be:

options.A: Treated as a regular railway servant from the date of his engagement
options.B: Entitled to confirmation in railway service on completion of his training
options.C: Deemed to be a probationer in railway service
options.D: A trainee and not a worker

e: Section 18 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 states that every apprentice undergoing apprenticeship training in a designated trade shall be a trainee and not a worker, so the engagement creates no right to regular employment or confirmation.

q: Under Section 89 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where a worker employed in a factory contracts any disease specified in the Third Schedule to the Act, the manager of the factory shall:

options.A: Merely grant leave to the worker for the period of his illness
options.B: Inform only the family members of the worker about the disease
options.C: Send a notice thereof to the prescribed authorities, including the Chief Inspector of Factories, in the prescribed form and manner
options.D: Take no action, as diseases contracted by workers are not covered by the Act

e: Section 89 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the manager, where a worker contracts a disease specified in the Third Schedule, to send a notice to the prescribed authorities, including the Chief Inspector, in the prescribed form and manner.

q: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 applies, among others, to the payment of wages to:

options.A: Only persons employed in factories registered under the Factories Act
options.B: Persons employed upon any railway by the railway administration, or by a person fulfilling a contract with the railway administration
options.C: Only persons holding civil posts under the Government
options.D: Only persons employed in mines and oil-fields

e: Section 1(4) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 applies the Act, among others, to persons employed upon any railway by the railway administration or by a person fulfilling a contract with the railway administration.

q: Under Section 13 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, effective and suitable provision is required to be made in every factory for securing and maintaining, in every workroom:

options.A: Adequate ventilation by the circulation of fresh air, and a temperature which will secure to the workers reasonable conditions of comfort and prevent injury to health
options.B: Air-conditioning of the workroom throughout the year
options.C: Only artificial lighting during the hours of work
options.D: Heating arrangements during the winter season only

e: Section 13 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires effective and suitable provision in every workroom for adequate ventilation by circulation of fresh air and for a temperature securing reasonable comfort and preventing injury to health.
